title: You don’t say “Send me”…
paragraphs:
You don’t say “Send me”…
until something inside you has been shattered.

Because pride doesn’t volunteer.
Pride negotiates.

“Use me… but on my terms.”
“Send me… but make it easy.”
“Call me… but don’t expose me.”
And that’s the part we skip.

Because before he ever said, “Here am I,”
he said something far more uncomfortable:
“Woe is me! For I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips…” — Isaiah 6:5
And that’s where the real story begins.

Because most of us want the calling…
but we avoid the crushing.

We want purpose without purification.
Assignment without altar.
Platform without repentance.

But we whisper,
“Just don’t touch that part of my life.”

That hidden pride.
That secret sin.
That quiet compromise no one sees.

You can sing in church
and still have unclean lips.

You can serve publicly
and still be broken privately.

You can say “Lord, Lord”
and still be holding back the one thing He’s asking for.

God is not impressed with availability
that refuses honesty.

Not slightly holy.
Not occasionally holy.
Completely.
“Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory.” — Isaiah 6:3

And when Isaiah saw that holiness,
he didn’t clap.

Because real encounters with God
don’t inflate your ego…

Some scholars interpret Isaiah’s “unclean lips” not just as personal sin, but as representing the sin of the people he belonged to—a shared brokenness, a collective rebellion. Whether personal or communal, the truth stands: when light shines, darkness is revealed.
Because God did not leave Isaiah in his shame.

He didn’t say,
“Clean yourself up, then come back.”
“Then one of the seraphim flew to me, having in his hand a live coal… and he touched my mouth with it and said: ‘Your guilt is taken away, and your sin atoned for.’” — Isaiah 6:6–7

Isaiah did not volunteer
until AFTER he was cleansed.
We say, “God, I’ll go—then maybe You can fix me on the way.”
But the pattern of Scripture is clear:
But the cross of Jesus Christ?
Because the truth is—your sin is deeper than dirty lips.
“The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately sick…” — Jeremiah 17:9
No amount of effort can purify that.
No religious routine can burn that away.
Not to make you slightly better.
“God made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.” — 2 Corinthians 5:21

Jesus took the fire of God’s holiness
so you wouldn’t be destroyed by it.

He absorbed the judgment
so you could receive mercy.
Not a coal touching your lips…
but a cross covering your life.
you don’t have to hide in shame.
You don’t have to negotiate with God anymore.
But here’s the question that remains:
Not your Sunday version of faith.

Because after Isaiah was cleansed,
God asked a question:
“Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” — Isaiah 6:8
And only THEN did Isaiah respond:
This was not a comfortable calling.
Isaiah would preach to people who would not listen.
He would speak truth in a culture that resisted God.
Because once you’ve truly encountered grace…
What are you still holding back?
What part of your life have you labeled “off-limits” to God?

Your habits?
Your relationships?
Your secret thoughts?
Your pride?

You can’t say “Send me”
while protecting what nailed Jesus to the cross.
Bring your sin into the light.
with clean hands and a surrendered heart—
Even if your future feels uncertain.
Even if obedience costs you everything.
Because the One who calls you…
is the One who saved you.
